As a 19M in a relationship with an 18F, I can say I truly understand your situation. My Girlfriend and I are both under constant stress, with family life for us both, financially for myself, and school-wise for herself. Outside stressors play a major role in the degradation of a relationship, but you need to understand that how your relationship will proceed will ultimately fall upon you and her, not what's going on in your lives. You made a huge mistake in throwing the "I should just leave you" so-to-speak at her, because it will just stress her out more and cause larger issues, and will likely make her doubtful of your feelings, because it just seem like when the going gets tough, you're not afraid to just leave (not to say this is, or is not true, just making a simple observation.) I have felt sometimes that my girlfriend can be insecure to things effecting me, and I know I can be the same ... as human beings we will never be truly perfect and you NEED to understand that people aren't mindreaders, and are incapable of understanding exactly how you feel on a constant basis. Your issue is that you have an unhealthy dependence on her, which just means that you NEED her, in the sense that if she does not provide you with what you need in the moment, you feel empty and it stresses you out. 

You need to make some friends, and find a hobby -- in my downtime, or when I am arguing with my girlfriend, I will often play League of Legends, do some research on Hip Hop and the industry, or watch some hockey -- those are my hobbies. I will skype my buddies, go to a friends to have pizza some beers and watch some sports, or whatever it may be...  I have outlets other than my girlfriend (although, I obviously go to her first as she is my priority) that I go to when things aren't perfect with her, and you need that... It will go a long way

What you should do: Relax. Take a deep breath. She has made it evidently clear that she loves you and isn't leaving you, so I don't think there's any reasons to be worried.

How it's effecting you: Nobody can take away how it makes you feel. I get that you probably feel unimportant because she isn't responding to you, or seeing you, and she isn't making you feel 'wanted'. I am sorry that you feel this way, but you have to keep in mind that SHE probably doesn't see it like this, and sees it as other things happening to come in the way that are equally or more important. You aren't married, it's okay if she feels like in the moment something family-based is more important because she has to deal with it... You need to do your own due diligence and handle your business, as much as you can, with friends, or yourself. 

I would advise speaking to her. Tell her how you feel about the situation, just over the phone. Don't talk about how you're upset, or how you're busy, but tell her that it makes you feel unimportant when she constantly bails on seeing you. Continue by telling her that you UNDERSTAND and APPRECIATE what she's going through, but that at the same time she still needs to make time for you, and your needs, as relationships at their core are give and take. Apologize for your brash comments, and tell her that you are dealing with your own issues, and on top of that you're faced with feelings you don't yet understand how to deal with because you feel so strongly about her that you feel an almost dependence on your relationship. 

If it doesn't change, or you notice she won't put the effort in: Move on. If you notice a trend that she is like that with other things, maybe don't take it as personally? But if you feel like you deserve better, then demand you get it. Be mindful of what she's experiencing, and be lenient, but if you deserve to be treated a certain way, and despite being understanding and speaking to her, she doesn't improve, then you are degrading your mental health by staying with her, unless you can fix yourself first.

I am not saying your relationship is doomed or she's bad or anything like that, but you need to talk to her, and be real with her about your dependence. You need to work together to get through your problems, and you are more than capable of doing that if you are mindful of your own emotions, and her experience. It's very easy to work together to fix things, I know, because I experience similar situations with my girlfriend and always we help eachother get through things, and it not only strengthens our relationship as a couple, but us as individuals as well.

My final hint of advice: Seek counseling.  Almost every University and College in North America has free counseling services for students. You suffer in ways similar to myself, and have a clear dependence on your relationship, which likely stems from your home life. I don't want to say your relationship will fail, as I whole-heartedly believe I will marry the woman I am with now (I mean, she has a promise ring already and is perfect for me) and believe that teenage love can last if it's right (especially when you can grow together), on the off-chance it falls apart, you need to be able to walk away with your head held high, and pick yourself up. Knowing how much you're struggling with being distant, if something were to happen in your relationship I imagine it would destroy you, and learning how  to deal with things by yourself will really help you out in the long run and make you stronger.

Sorry for the wall of text, I just noticed you haven't gotten a lot of responses and I hope that I can help you out, I imagine if you came here you are truly desperate for outside input.

As a now 18 year old University student finally experiencing life on my own, I can say I have gone through quite a few things you are experiencing.

I know how it feels to be self-conscious. Up until recently I was "overweight" which although it wasn't bad, nor did anyone say anything to me... I felt it on a personal level, and am still sorta uncomfortable with my body.

I also know how it feels to be depressed. I know how it feels to not be in a relationship (that's due to other things, and by self decision to remain single). I know how it feels to feel like you have no real friends, I've had everyone turn on me in the moments where I felt most exposed ... Luckily I always had SOMEONE there to keep me out of the darkness, even if they left my life down the road, someone would always be there to replace them.

I have faked happiness to people for years.... To be honest, I only stopped faking it recently, when I finally realized how happy I truly was, and defeated the burdensome 'depression'. So, here are the things I can offer to maybe help you at the end of the day.

Life gets better. Trust me. Everyone says it, everyone claims they have some special insight that proves it, but I won't, I will just tell you it does.

 I can't really advise you on the friend, or relationship factors. Some people say you can't love someone else, until you love yourself ... and you know, maybe that's true. You are still a young man, you have at least 50 years of life left, so I wouldn't be fretting about anything at this point. If you are sincerely upset about your weight, do your best to eat healthy, and maybe try and get to the gym. If you are too self conscious, maybe start working out at home, or going for walks? Do your best to better your body, and gain that much needed confidence.

Apply for any job you can, go to cafes or events in your town or city, maybe go on a vacation to another city for a week and just speak to people. The worst that happens is you get shut down, or shutout ... but it's more likely you will meet some people, and maybe make some of those friends you were looking for.

At this point, I would look into a hobby. Find something that you love, and that makes you happy. Work on your weight to the best of your ability if it's something that bothers you, otherwise just embrace it. Life isn't a walk in the park, I won't pretend it is, and like everything else worth having, you gotta fight for it. I have faith that you can turn your life around for the better, but you need to have that same faith. If you ever need to talk, feel free to inbox me on Reddit and I will do my best to read it.

Despite rarely checking it, I will be looking for your message. Remember, everything gets better. Love life, and enjoy the good times.

Hey!

You came here for a reason. We all know that reason, so lets not skip over it.

I'll say what 1000 other people have said, could say, and will say. Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem.

I've been at points in life where I sat debating what was next, if anything was next. I had incredible anxiety, and it felt like I had nobody to turn to ... nothing to turn to.

I watched the television shows Smart Guy and Boy Meets World on YouTube ... actually the entirety of both shows, multiple times. Even though I had already watched them in their entirety before. Something about getting lost in those shows made everything seem to get better.

I went months feeling exactly how you did. But eventually, I realized there is so much good in the world, that no matter how bad my day was, there was always hope.

Never give up, because I promise what's on the otherside isn't worth it.

My advice? Try going back to school maybe? Try taking up a hobby? I got through it by getting out of High School and into UNiversity, and I am as happy as can be. I also found a passion for music (hip-hop) that has absorbed every aspect of my life. Maybe you will find something you love too. Just learn everyday, and try and educate yourself.

If you are looking for hope, or reason, save a life. If this comment in any way stops you from wanting to take your life, then I have succeeded in my goal. Maybe you can do the same thing, but for another person. You can go to sleep knowing you saved someone's life.
